summary: During the meeting, the team discussed various aspects of the project, including tool training, project plan, and design features. The team decided to set the selling price at 25 Euros (17 Pounds) with a production cost of 12.5 Euros, aiming for a profit of 50 million Euros in the first year (decided by the Project Manager). Marketing will target an international market with a focus on user-friendly design for all age groups. Action items include the Project Manager pulling up and sharing pricing details immediately and the Marketing team considering the menu display for the remote control design for the next meeting. The team also decided to explore a flip top remote control design and a dual function menu with basic and advanced controls. The Industrial Designer suggested a space-saving design using plastic for cost-effectiveness. The Project Manager will own the task of evaluating these features with a deadline of the next meeting in half an hour. The team agreed to shift focus to individual tasks before the next meeting and reconsider the necessity of a fashionable design.

During the meeting, the team discussed various aspects of the remote control design, including universal control design, marketing insights, and user interface features. The group decided to continue with a flip-top design and use infrared signals, ensuring the design is user-friendly. Action items were assigned: Marketing will provide market research data, the Industrial Designer will finalize the circuit design, and the User Interface will develop a prototype. The plan was adjusted to focus on TV functions only due to budget constraints, and Marketing will conduct further research on speech recognition and LCD display features.

The team also addressed remote control functions, deciding to focus on T_V_ and video functions, and to include a rechargeable battery with a docking station. Marketing proposed adding a reminder feature on the LCD, but the Project Manager suggested considering it as an advertisement. The team agreed to review instruction manuals for simplicity and relevance. Action items were set for Marketing to prepare a questionnaire for the manuals by the end of the day. The meeting extended to discuss further plans during lunchtime.

During the meeting, the team discussed various aspects of the product design, including conceptual design, market trends, and specific features. Key decisions included removing the voice recognition feature and opting for standard double A and triple A batteries. Action items were assigned to the Industrial Designer and User Interface for investigating kinetic charging options and evaluating battery life, respectively. The team also decided to incorporate a flip design with a compact mirror inside and a rubber cover for the remote to enhance user comfort. Proposals for adding an attachment to the closing feature and using a printed circuit board (PCB) for the remote control were considered but not immediately implemented. The focus shifted to using kinetic charging, watch-type batteries, and an LCD display on the top side of the flip top. The team agreed on using fruit and vegetable colors for the rubber cover and a plastic case with a rubberized exterior. Voice recognition or a whistle were proposed as alternatives to the beeper for location. Action items were set for the User Interface to check the feasibility of voice recognition and for Marketing to finalize the branding strategy.

During the meeting, the team discussed prototype design, evaluation criteria, and various proposals. Key decisions included using a standard chip and stand-by function, incorporating voice recognition software, and evaluating the prototype using a 7-point scale. Action items were assigned to the Industrial Designer and User Interface for a prototype presentation and evaluation ratings by the next meeting. The team also decided to use regular batteries instead of kinetic cells to reduce costs. In the second segment, the focus was on ease of use, cost evaluation, and material usage. Decisions were made to use a single double-curved plastic and rubber case, and to proceed with the prototype based on evaluation findings. Action items were assigned to the Industrial Designer and Project Manager to ensure the prototype design and update cost calculations. The team decided to use standard batteries to simplify the design. In the third segment, discussions centered on pricing, budget, and future project directions. The team agreed to keep the price at 12.25 Euros and to present a budget increase proposal to head office. Action items were assigned to Marketing and Project Manager to prepare the proposal and delegate tasks. The final segment covered the completion of a final questionnaire and discussed celebration plans, though no specific plans were decided.

The meeting focused on the initial planning and division of tasks for the new remote control project. The team decided that Industrial Designer Kate would handle the functional design, User Interface Steph would manage the technical functions, and Marketing would develop the user requirements specification. The remote control design would be inspired by an animal, with a cat, rat, and fish being suggested. The team agreed to keep the design simple and user-friendly, avoiding unnecessary buttons. The project aims to sell 4 million remote controls at 25 Euros each to achieve a profit of 50 million Euros. The production cost is set at 12.5 Euros per item. The next steps involve individual work on the designs, with a deadline to be determined. The team agreed to meet again to review progress.

During the meeting, the team discussed the functional design of remote controls, new project requirements, and market research findings. Key decisions included focusing on essential functions (channel, volume, enter) and considering speech recognition for early adopters. The team agreed to limit the remote control to TV functions only. Action items were assigned: User Interface to research existing remote controls and speech recognition, Marketing to gather more market research, and Project Manager to send out a competitive analysis. The plan was adjusted to prioritize a simpler, mass-produced design over speech recognition. The team also decided to target a younger age range and streamline the user interface with a turning dial for on/off. Action items were set for Industrial Designer, User Interface, and Marketing to work on components, user interface design, and trend-watching, respectively. The meeting concluded with a plan to adjust the meeting time and add individual work time to ensure completion within the allocated 40 minutes.

During the meeting, the team reviewed previous minutes and discussed marketing research, component design, and energy sources. The group agreed to explore spongy, fruit and veg-themed covers for the remote control, with titanium considered as a material. The Industrial Designer was tasked with describing the components and their limitations, while Marketing was to finalize the name and concept for the covers. The team decided to focus on a simple, cost-effective design with push buttons and an LCD display, opting for a plastic or rubber remote due to manufacturing constraints. Marketing and User Interface agreed to present detailed interface design options and finalize color and style choices, respectively. The group also decided to use kinetic energy for the remote control and a plastic case with a spongy cover. Action items were assigned to User Interface for look and feel design, Steph for user interface design, and Marketing for product evaluation, all with deadlines set for the next meeting. The meeting was rescheduled to start in 30 minutes instead of 10.

During the meeting, the team reviewed previous minutes and presented two prototype designs: one curved and one banana-shaped. The Industrial Designer suggested placing the on-off button in the back for ease of use. The group decided to opt for a minimalistic design with prominent buttons and considered both hard plastic and spongy rubber options for the remote. User Interface was tasked with developing programming for menus and text boxes, while Marketing was to finalize evaluation criteria and conduct the evaluation. The team shifted focus to a more minimalistic design with an emphasis on functionality over complexity. They decided to use the banana shape or a curved blob design and named the product "E_F" (Elegant, Fancy). The product was evaluated as "technologically innovative" (False), "easy to use" (True), "trendy" (2-3), "attractive" (True), and "cost saving" (True). User Interface was assigned to develop the button interface and programming, and Marketing was to finalize the product name and marketing strategy. The team also discussed the final questionnaire, meeting summary, and a product launch party, with Marketing responsible for saving all files in the correct directories immediately. No changes to the plan were made, but ice sculptures and the product launch party were briefly discussed.

During the meeting, the team discussed the design and features of a new remote control. The main topics included the project overview, design phases, and feature ideas. User Interface proposed a universal remote with tracking features, while Marketing suggested a modern, user-friendly design. Industrial Designer and UI discussed a compromise between a spherical design and practicality. The team decided to aim for a modern, user-friendly, and sturdy design, considering a ball-shaped design with a flat bottom and exploring a hinge or keyboard-type design.

Action items were assigned: UI to draw the ball idea with internal buttons by the next meeting, Marketing to draw a keyboard-type or hinge design by the next meeting, and the Project Manager to summarize and document the design ideas by the end of the day. The plan was adjusted to focus on a flat design with grips on the sides, eliminating the ball function, and adding sensors on both sides for directionality, though this was later dropped due to cost concerns.

During the meeting, the team discussed the design and functionality of a new remote control, focusing on user-centered design and multifunctionality. Key decisions included prioritizing a modern, user-friendly appearance and a one-handed, thumb-friendly design. The team agreed to incorporate a two-in-one remote concept and limit the remote to TV functions only. Action items were assigned: Ryan to finalize the design concept and present it by the end of the week, Manuel to work on components, and both Ryan and Manuel to explore user interaction with the proposed designs. The project manager also decided to focus on component design and user interaction for the next meeting. The plan was adjusted to address initial technical issues and to streamline the design process.

During the meeting, the team reviewed previous minutes and focused on the goal of creating the finest remote control, emphasizing a fancy look-and-feel, technological innovation, and ease of use. Decisions were made to incorporate a two-piece design, speech recognition technology, and a simple user interface. Action items were assigned: Marketing will research and incorporate fashion trends into the design, User Interface will develop a prototype, and Industrial Designer will provide detailed component design. The plan was changed to use a basic battery as the energy source, removing the need for a base station and incorporating a rubbery supplement into the case design. The team also decided to finalize the design with a banana shape and grey stripes, and to provide detailed cost estimates for materials and components.

During the meeting, the team discussed the prototype design, budget, and user feedback. The prototype was proposed to be a banana-shaped remote with a scroll wheel and LCD screen, but speech recognition was decided against due to budget constraints. The team agreed to add an on-off button for convenience. Action items include evaluating the prototype, finalizing the budget, and integrating an anti-theft feature. The team also decided to use a 50% profit margin, set the price at €300, and remove the LCD display, opting for a scroll wheel interface instead. The Industrial Designer will redesign the remote control, and the Project Manager will complete the project evaluation. The budget was reduced from €17 to €15.50 by removing the LCD display and LCD screen, and the team agreed to use a hand dynamo instead of a battery.

The team discussed the design of a new remote control, focusing on its functional, conceptual, and detailed design. The remote control will be original, trendy, and user-friendly, with a target price of 25 Euros for an international market aiming to sell two million units at a production cost of 12.50 Euros. The remote control will be robust, child-proof, and colorful, with a single color scheme. It will be small and have minimal buttons, with the option to change colors. The team decided to keep the remote control simple, with only three main functions, and include features like a go-back button and history. The next meeting will be in 30 minutes, where they will prioritize the ideas and delve into technical aspects. Action items include each team member working on their specific roles, with Marketing to develop user requirement specifications. The meeting concluded with clear next steps and deadlines.

During the meeting, the team discussed key topics including user needs, technical functions, and design principles. Sammy Benjo proposed focusing on user feedback and preferences, while Mark Dwight suggested simplifying the design. The team decided to target young users for the speech recognition feature and prioritize simplicity in design. Action items were assigned: Mark Dwight is to design a simplified remote control prototype by next week, and Sammy Benjo is to conduct user surveys on remote control preferences by the end of the month. The team also decided to focus on a TV remote control first, then expand to a universal remote, and incorporated speech recognition into the design.

The discussion then shifted to the design and functionality of a baby-proof remote control, universal remote capabilities, and technical aspects. The team decided to focus on a TV remote control initially, with Industrial Designer Mark Dwight to input connections and components on the whiteboard by the next meeting. Action items included Marketing to research if people need specific channel control by the end of the week and Industrial Designer to explore clap or whistle as a control method by the end of the week.

In the final segment, the team proposed concepts for a remote control that can be controlled by shouting commands and considered adding a clap or whistle feature. The Project Manager decided to focus on components and individual actions in the next meeting. The team agreed to use a simple beep as a response to commands and to shift focus to individual components and personalization features in the upcoming session.

During the meeting, the team discussed key topics including conceptual design, component concepts, user interface design, pricing, design trends, and features of the remote control. The main decisions were to use a simple battery and titanium design, integrate an LCD display for information only, and include speech recognition. Marketing proposed making the remote control optional, with a pink option for young people, and suggested adding light features and smart functionalities like speech and fingerprint recognition. The team decided to follow general trends like fruit and vegetable designs and to focus on the "fancy" feature for differentiation. Action items were assigned to the Industrial Designer and User Interface to explore titanium and spongy fruit-shaped options, and to the Marketing team to confirm the "fancy" feature. The Project Manager decided to stick with LCD for information display and two batteries. The plan was adjusted to emphasize fewer, more functional buttons and to follow general design trends rather than just remote control trends.

During the meeting, the team discussed prototype evaluation, remote control features, and project budgeting. The group decided to use a 1-7 scale for evaluating the prototype, with Marketing leading the evaluation. The Project Manager proposed a party to celebrate success, which was agreed upon. Industrial Designer was tasked with presenting the prototype and technical specifications, while Marketing would lead the evaluation. The team also decided to use two directional buttons, a jog wheel for cursor control, and a titanium case for the remote control. User Interface suggested a fruit design for aesthetics but acknowledged practicality concerns. The Project Manager proposed switching to a hand dynamo for power, reducing battery needs. The team agreed to put a minus two on the chip feature, and they decided to stick to the original plan to stay within the budget. The meeting concluded with a plan to celebrate the project's success and to continue working on the design and functionality improvements.

During the meeting, the team discussed the development of a new television remote control, focusing on design, project management, and technical considerations. The Project Manager proposed a three-stage design process and set a selling price of 25 Euros with a profit target of 50 million Euros, emphasizing international markets and production costs under 12.50 Euros. The Industrial Designer suggested inter-operability and Bluetooth communication, while the User Interface proposed a simple animal drawing on the SMARTboard and basic technical functions like a touch-screen or stick control.

Key decisions included using infrared control for simplicity and compatibility, ensuring buttons are visible in dark conditions, and limiting power consumption. Action items were assigned: the User Interface to document glow-in-the-dark buttons, the Industrial Designer to explore stick control options, and the Project Manager to summarize the meeting points and distribute them to the team. The plan was adjusted to include a tool training session and a presentation section. No significant changes were proposed, but the team agreed on the use of infrared control and a simple display for functions.

During the meeting, the team discussed the new project requirements and individual presentations on remote control design. Key decisions were made to exclude teletext support, focus on customers under 40, and prioritize ease-of-use over multi-functionality. The Industrial Designer decided to implement infrared communication and energy-friendly components, while the User Interface proposed a sound signal feature for easier button location. Action items were assigned: the User Interface to finalize the ease-of-use design by the end of the week, the Industrial Designer to develop the design scheme and research the sound signal feature, and Marketing to conduct market research on the target group. The team also decided to focus on basic functions and prioritize channel selection, volume control, and teletext. The Industrial Designer will design a round button for advanced functions, and the User Interface will finalize the function list. The team agreed to shift focus to a younger audience while considering older users and explore cheaper design options, including voice recognition and a cradle for recharging.

During the meeting, the team discussed key topics including remote control design, energy consumption, user interface, and voice recognition. The team decided to focus on younger user preferences and design elements, shifting the emphasis to innovation, color, and soft materials. The Project Manager summarized that innovation, color, and soft materials are the most important aspects and decided to make presentations and discuss remote control concepts.

Action items were assigned: the Industrial Designer is to present on casing shapes and materials by the next meeting, the User Interface team will present on voice recognition and interface design by the next meeting, and the Marketing team will provide updated market findings by the next meeting.

The team also decided to use rubber with colors for the remote control design, skip the titanium casing and use wood or spongy materials, and integrate scroll-wheels with push-buttons while ensuring compatibility with the regular chip. The Project Manager decided to use traditional batteries and solar power as complementary energy sources and to use a single-curved case with grey and yellow corporate colors.

Changes to the plan included shifting from a titanium casing to wood or spongy materials, integrating scroll-wheels with push-buttons, and using the sample sensor and speaker for voice recognition. The Industrial Designer is to finalize the remote control design with the chosen materials and components by the end of the week, and the User Interface team is to research and propose designs for the remote control buttons and scroll-wheels by the next meeting.

During the meeting, the team discussed the design and usability of the remote control, product rating, project process evaluation, and tools used. The Industrial Designer proposed using a scroll bar and voice recognition feature, while Marketing suggested adding two programming buttons and a voice recognition disable button. Project Manager agreed to use these features but decided to remove the solar cell to keep costs under €12.50. The team agreed to evaluate the prototype's design and usability, with User Interface tasked to finalize the design by the next meeting, and Project Manager to evaluate it by the following week. The team decided to give the remote control a "one" rating, with User Interface to calculate the overall rating by the next meeting. The Project Manager also decided to introduce a radar function and consider a higher selling price of around 50 Euros. The team acknowledged limited creativity due to cost constraints and suggested better communication between meetings. The discussion also included evaluating SMARTboards, proposing an OCR feature, and redesigning the product to be simple and one-coloured. The team agreed to redesign the product and ensure it can be easily shared and used, with deadlines set for the next meeting. The Project Manager also planned to introduce a feature for easily selecting and distributing slides, though this was not implemented due to lack of explanation.
